**Finding: missing (high severity) — no Customer termination for convenience.**

- Section 9 contains only for-cause (9.1), insolvency (9.2), and security/SLA/legal-violation (9.3) termination rights, plus the Order-Form-severability rule in 9.5. Neither party has a convenience right anywhere in the document (a full-text search for "convenience" returns only the unrelated purchase-order language in § 1.6).
- Section 8.1 commits us to a three-year term with 12-month auto-renewals (8.2, on 180 days' notice), so the absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation.
- On the positive side, Vendor has no convenience right either, so no deletion is needed — only a confirmation that it gains none.

**Redline (validated, preferred position):** new Section 9.4 after 9.3 giving Customer a 30-day convenience right, in whole or in part, without penalty or early-termination fee, with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees keyed to the existing refund mechanics in Section 10.2, and confirming Vendor has no convenience right during a committed term. The comment offers 60 days' notice as a fallback if Vendor pushes back.
